criteria.name: j01_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J01: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says each shift limit is read from Appendix A by the start time in UK local time and the number of ward assignments.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note explicitly states: “For SHIFT and EXTENSION findings, the limit comes from Appendix A, read by the start time in UK local time and the number of ward assignments.” This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria.name: j02_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J02: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a transfer from another site before ward work counts as an assignment under Revision 7 and not under Revision 6.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly states: 'under Rev 7 a transfer from another site counts as a ward assignment; under Rev 6 it does not.' It also applies this rule to SSF-00023, counting three wards plus the transfer as four assignments.

criteria.name: j03_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J03: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says an extension limit is the Appendix A maximum plus the revision's allowance, two hours under Revision 6 and ninety minutes under Revision 7.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note identifies the extension allowance as 2:00 under Revision 6 and 1:30 under Revision 7. Its EXTENSION findings explicitly add those allowances to the Appendix A maximum, for example 660 + 120 = 780 under Rev 6 and 720 + 90 = 810 under Rev 7.

criteria.name: j04_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J04: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says an extension stands only when a shift extension authorisation is filed and signed by the site manager.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note treats unsigned authorisations (SEA-6991) and unfiled extensions (AM-1017-MGH-852) as invalid, but it never states that the authorisation must be signed by the site manager. It therefore does not fully state the required rule.

criteria.name: j05_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J05: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says minimum rest is the preceding duty period and not less than eleven hours.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note states: “For REST findings, the limit is the preceding duty period (shift plus 30 minutes of handover), with a floor of 660.” Since 660 minutes is eleven hours, this explicitly satisfies the criterion.

criteria.name: j06_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J06: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says Revision 7 adds the length of a site manager's extension to the rest that follows it.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note explicitly states: “Rest after an extension: under Rev 7 (rule 5.3), the minimum rest after an authorised extension grows by the extension's length.” It also illustrates this with SSF-00003, adding a 45-minute extension to 735 minutes of duty to yield a 780-minute rest requirement.

criteria.name: j07_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J07: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the rolling-hours limits are tested over rolling windows of consecutive days, not calendar weeks.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note says it slid 7-, 14-, and 28-day windows across every end date from 1 to 28 October, including earlier data to complete early-October windows. This clearly describes rolling windows of consecutive days rather than calendar weeks.

criteria.name: j08_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J08: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says on-call served on site counts in full and on-call from home counts as one quarter.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. In final_message.md under “How I tested the rolling-hours limits,” the note explicitly states that “on-call served on site counts in full” and “on-call from home counts as a quarter of its length.”

criteria.name: j09_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J09: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a shift's revision is decided by its start time in UK local time.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly states that each shift’s UTC start time is converted to UK local time and that Rev 6 applies before 00:00 local on 15 October, with Rev 7 applying from then onward. It also rejects roster day, UTC date, and shift-reference date as the basis for selecting the revision.

criteria.name: j10_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J10: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note rejects the UTC date as the test of which revision applies.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly states, “I ruled out deciding by the roster day, by the UTC date, or by the date in the shift reference.” It instead determines the applicable revision using each shift’s start time converted to UK local time and the local-midnight cutoff on 15 October.

criteria.name: j11_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J11: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note rejects the roster day as the test of which revision applies.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note explicitly states, “I ruled out deciding by the roster day,” and instead applies revisions using each shift’s start time in UK local time. It reinforces this with AM-1015-MGH-283: although its roster day is 15 October, its local start was 23:20 on 14 October, so Rev 6 applies.

criteria.name: j12_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J12: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a ward timesheet photograph replaced a shift-actuals clock-out time.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note says it set aside actuals in favor of timesheet pages: TS-10088 shows clock-out corrected to 22:14 against the actuals' 18:01, and TS-28498 shows clock-out corrected from 18:35 to 19:36. It also states that the corrected timesheet pages were checked against the images and filed as corrections.

criteria.name: j13_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J13: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a ward timesheet photograph showed a ward assignment the shift-actuals record omitted.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note states that timesheet TS-10088 shows a fifth ward assignment, whereas the shift-actuals record lists only four. It also confirms the corrected timesheet pages were checked against the images, establishing that the photograph revealed an omitted ward assignment.

criteria.name: j14_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J14: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says an extension authorisation stood although the shift-actuals extension flag said no.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly states that SEA-1377 was a signed authorisation although the actuals said no extension was used. It applies that authorisation to AM-1017-MGH-354 as an EXTENSION finding with an 810-minute limit, demonstrating that the authorisation stood over the shift-actuals extension flag.

criteria.name: j15_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J15: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says an extension recorded in the shift actuals without a filed authorisation was treated as no extension.
criteria.reasoning: Yes. The closing note explicitly states for AM-1017-MGH-852 (45172): “the actuals say an extension was used but ‘not filed’, and the register holds no authorisation, so it counts as no extension.”

criteria.name: j16_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J16: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a bleep-log note moved a shift's start to a call-in with a transfer from another site.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note identifies BL-119 for AM-1018-MGH-628 as a call-in from on-call at home with a transfer from Westbrook General, changing the start to 07:23 UTC rather than 09:00. This explicitly satisfies the criterion.

criteria.name: j17_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J17: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says a hospital tannoy announcement in a bleep-log note showed on-call the roster booked at home was served on site.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly states that BL-717 records on-call rostered at home, but a hospital public-address announcement in the background showed it was served on site. It also identifies BL-668 as the same situation, with a hospital announcement in the background.

criteria.name: j18_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J18: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says last week's roster export was not used.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly lists the roster export among sources disregarded, stating that it is out of date and has an '.old' address for nurse 31279. This confirms that the outdated roster export was not used.

criteria.name: j21_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J21: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the staff side representative's view was set aside because it carries no standing.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note explicitly says it disregarded the staff side's draft local agreement because 'a draft has no effect under SS-4 and your rules.' This states that the staff side's position was set aside for having no standing.

criteria.name: j22_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J22: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the draft local agreement was set aside because it is unsigned and has no effect.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note says the draft local agreement was disregarded because a draft has no effect under SS-4 and the user's rules, but it does not state that the agreement was unsigned. Thus it does not satisfy both required elements.

criteria.reasoning: The closing note says the pre-15-October actuals archive refused queries, but it does not say its records were read one by one. Instead, it says searching by staff number returned each nurse’s complete roster and actuals records, including archived records, in one call each.

criteria.name: j24_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru

criteria.name: j26_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J26: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note reports a finding that is not among the run's own finding records.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note reports 32 recorded findings and lists all 32 with finding references SSF-00001 through SSF-00032. It does not claim an additional finding outside that set. The September rolling-hours exceedance is explicitly excluded, and the alternative extension calculation is presented as hypothetical, not as another recorded finding. Differences from the reference [REDACTED]ution do not establish that the note reports a finding absent from the run's own records.

criteria.name: j30_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J30: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note states a chapter 7 limit value that contradicts the revision it names.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note does not state a chapter 7 limit that contradicts its named revision. Its revision-specific Appendix A limits and extension allowances agree with the reference, including the reduced Rev 7 05:00–05:59 limits and the 90-minute extension allowance. Other discrepancies in the audit do not establish this particular contradiction.

criteria.name: j31_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J31: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note dates the change of revision to anything other than 00:00 UK local time on 15 October 2026.
criteria.reasoning: No. The closing note explicitly states that shifts starting before 00:00 UK local time on 15 October fall under Rev 6 and shifts from that moment onward fall under Rev 7. Thus it dates the revision change to the specified time, not to anything else.

The titles therefore meet the readability criterion without relying on their properties or notices.

criteria.reasoning: The trajectory shows roster queries and per-staff record counts, but no comparison of the retrieved roster listing against the database's stated row count. The run does not visibly obtain the roster database's stated total or reconcile it with the listing.

criteria.name: j39_judge_from_trajectory_md_the_run_s
criteria.description: J39: judge from trajectory.md (the run's steps in order). The trajectory shows the run reading archived actuals record by record after the archive query was refused.
criteria.reasoning: The trajectory does not show an archived-actuals database query being refused and then archived actuals being read record by record. Instead, steps 25–54 retrieve actuals through searches by staff number. The refusal at step 15 is a rate limit on the nurse-register query, not an archive query, and the occasional later get_page calls do not establish the required sequence.

criteria.reasoning: Step 15 shows query_database for db-nurse-register with start_cursor "200" failing with a 429 rate-limit response. Step 17 retries the same query with identical parameters, and step 18 confirms that its 100 returned records were ingested.

criteria.name: j42_judge_from_trajectory_md_the_run_s

criteria.name: j46_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J46: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). For every finding in the reference, without exception, the note names the rule that set its limit and states its limit, actual and excess minutes as the reference gives them; answer no if any reference finding is missing or any of those figures differs.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note omits two reference findings: nurse 38571, AM-1021-MGH-259 SHIFT (limit 720, actual 764, excess 44 minutes), and nurse 49301, AM-1004-MGH-545 SHIFT (limit 780, actual 801, excess 21 minutes). It also reports incorrect figures for nurse 49301, AM-1008-MGH-741 REST: 793/772/21 instead of the reference's limit/actual/excess of 831/734/97. For nurse 37488, AM-1025-MGH-348, it records SHIFT with 720/850/130 rather than the reference's EXTENSION with 810/850/40; mentioning the correct figures only as a hypothetical alternative does not correctly state the reference finding.
